assessment.subject: GHK-Cu peptide (glycyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine)
assessment.object: tissue repair and multiple health conditions
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review claims the GHK-Cu peptide has broad regenerative, protective, anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory health benefits across many tissues.

assessment.subject: Selank (heptapeptide)
assessment.claim_summary: In vitro radioligand binding study reports Selank acts as a positive allosteric modulator of GABA receptor binding.

assessment.subject: Melanotan (melanocortin analogue)
assessment.claim_summary: Case report describes acute low-flow priapism following subcutaneous melanotan injection in one patient.

assessment.subject: BPC 157 (pentadecapeptide)
assessment.object: musculoskeletal soft tissue healing (tendon, ligament, muscle)
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review concludes BPC 157 consistently promotes soft-tissue healing in animal models, with efficacy not yet confirmed in humans.

assessment.subject: Liraglutide and semaglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonists)
assessment.claim_summary: Review chronicles the design and development of GLP-1 analogs liraglutide and semaglutide and summarizes their effects on glycemic control, weight and cardiovascular outcomes.

assessment.subject: Exendin-4 analogs (GLP-1 analog tracers)
assessment.claim_summary: Review overviews the development and clinical use of exendin-4-based tracers for imaging and therapy of insulinomas via GLP-1 receptor targeting.

assessment.subject: Eruptive melanocytic nevi
assessment.claim_summary: Systematic review of 179 published EMN cases identifies triggers (skin diseases 50%, immunosuppressants/chemotherapy/melanotan 41%) and proposes a clinical subclassification.
assessment.magnitude: drugs/chemotherapy/melanotan suspected cause in ~41% of cases

assessment.subject: Bremelanotide (MC4R agonist)
assessment.claim_summary: Regulatory approval note summarizing the development milestones of bremelanotide, an MC4R agonist approved in the USA for premenopausal HSDD.

assessment.subject: Intrathecal drug delivery systems (IDDS)
assessment.claim_summary: Review of intrathecal drug delivery systems summarizing their established efficacy for chronic pain and spasticity and updated technical and pharmacological recommendations.

assessment.subject: Elamipretide (SS-31)
assessment.object: LPS-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and memory impairment in mice
assessment.claim_summary: Controlled mouse study reports the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant elamipretide attenuates LPS-induced mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation and memory impairment.

assessment.subject: ACE inhibitors
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review of ACE-inhibitor-associated angioedema covering its ~0.1-0.7% prevalence, ethnic predisposition, bradykinin-mediated pathogenesis and debated treatments.
assessment.magnitude: ACEi-AE occurs in 0.1-0.7% of treated patients

assessment.subject: Melanotan II (melanocortin receptor agonist)
assessment.claim_summary: Case report with literature review presents a case of renal infarction most likely attributable to Melanotan II and discusses possible thrombotic and toxic mechanisms.

assessment.subject: Selank and Semax (neuropeptides)
assessment.claim_summary: Placebo-controlled fMRI study in 52 healthy participants reports Selank and Semax alter resting-state functional connectivity between the right amygdala and right temporal cortex.

assessment.subject: Selank (neuropeptide)
assessment.object: pro-/anti-inflammatory cytokines under social stress in rats
assessment.claim_summary: Controlled rat social-stress study reports stress raises IL-1b, IL-6 and TGF-b1 and that the neuropeptides reduce these cytokines toward control levels, indicating stress-protective activity.

assessment.subject: Tirzepatide (dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist)
assessment.object: GIP and GLP-1 receptor signaling and biased agonism
assessment.claim_summary: Mechanistic pharmacology study reports tirzepatide is an imbalanced dual agonist favoring the GIP receptor and shows biased GLP-1 receptor signaling, potentially explaining its metabolic efficacy.

assessment.subject: Setmelanotide (MC4R agonist)
assessment.object: severe obesity due to POMC or LEPR deficiency
assessment.claim_summary: Two single-arm open-label phase 3 trials (n=21) report setmelanotide produced >=10% weight loss in 80% (POMC) and 45% (LEPR) of participants and significantly reduced hunger scores at ~1 year.
assessment.magnitude: 80% (POMC) and 45% (LEPR) achieved >=10% weight loss at ~1 year

assessment.subject: Exendin-4 / exenatide (GLP-1 receptor agonist)
assessment.claim_summary: Review of preclinical and clinical evidence for the GLP-1 receptor agonist exendin-4 (exenatide) as a potential therapy for Parkinson's disease.

assessment.subject: Tirzepatide (dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist)
assessment.claim_summary: 40-week double-blind randomized placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (SURPASS-1, n=478) shows tirzepatide monotherapy reduces HbA1c by up to ~2.1% and body weight by 7-9.5 kg versus placebo without increased hypoglycemia.
assessment.magnitude: HbA1c treatment difference up to -2.11% vs placebo; 7.0-9.5 kg weight loss

assessment.subject: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) and related peptides
assessment.claim_summary: Review of the mechanisms by which parathyroid hormone and PTH-related peptides regulate bone formation and resorption, and prospects for improved PTH-related peptide therapeutics.

assessment.subject: Irritable bowel syndrome
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review of irritable bowel syndrome covering its ~5-10% prevalence, unknown pathophysiology, clinical features, diagnosis and dietary/pharmacological/psychotherapeutic management.

assessment.subject: BPC 157 (stable gastric pentadecapeptide)
assessment.object: wound healing across skin and multiple tissues
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review claims BPC 157 promotes healing of skin and diverse other tissue wounds with no reported toxicity, based largely on rat studies.

assessment.subject: Intra-articular BPC 157 (with or without thymosin beta-4)
assessment.claim_summary: Small uncontrolled retrospective chart review (17 patients, phone survey) reports 87.5% experienced knee-pain relief after intra-articular BPC 157 (91.6% with BPC 157 alone).
assessment.magnitude: 87.5% (14/16) reported knee-pain relief; 91.6% with BPC 157 alone
